Subject: MSA Security exhibit — audit rights & evidence process (HealthScope)

Hi Mina,

Thanks for the call earlier. As we pull final language for the MSA/order form we want to confirm a few security exhibit items from Redwood so we can route the order to procurement: 

- SOC 2: we expect a SOC 2 Type II report within the past 12 months and a primary contact for questions about scope.
- Pen test: we need an explicit process for vendor penetration testing — a test plan submission, approval window and a safe harbor to avoid service disruption.
- Audit rights: please confirm what you expect for inspection windows, notice periods, and whether you provide sampled evidence sets or full export on request. For regulated workflows we typically require a 30-day scheduling notice and a 3-business-day on-site or remote inspection window per quarter.
- Evidence cadence: a matrix of who owns evidence (Redwood/Customer) and where artifacts (logs, configs, attestation) will be uploaded.

Can you send a short draft security exhibit and a proposed evidence cadence? Procurement also asked for an explicit redline we can attach to the order form to expedite legal review.

Attached: HS_SOC2-scope-map.xlsx (control mapping we expect).

Appreciate a quick turnaround — procurement would like this in the week. If easier, happy to jump on a 30-minute call.

Thanks,
Lauren

Subject: Re: MSA Security exhibit — audit rights & evidence process (HealthScope)

Hi Lauren — thanks for the clear list. Attaching a working draft of the security exhibit and an evidence ownership matrix that maps each artifact to Redwood (service logs, change logs, pen-test reports) or customer-deliverable (config screenshots, signed attestation).

High-level proposals from engineering and security:
- SOC2: we'll provide our most recent SOC 2 Type II report and a named contact (Karthik on legal for scope questions, and myself for operational clarifications).
- Pen test coordination: Redwood requires a test-plan submission at least 21 calendar days before the proposed window. We will review and provide written approval or requested modifications within 7 business days. Tests must be limited to agreed targets and scheduling with our SRE on-call; we prohibit testing that could cause degradation of production services (we'll provide a safe-harbor checklist).
- Inspection windows: propose a standard of 30 calendar days' notice for a compliance inspection and a 3 business day evidence collection window per 12-month period for vendor-initiated reviews; for annual or full-scope audits we can negotiate a separate schedule.
- Evidence cadence: suggest quarterly evidence sprints where we upload sampled artifacts into a shared folder and provide a one-hour review call. If HealthScope requests a deeper export, we ask for a formal legal request and offer a redaction/filtered log export; full exports require a court-order or agreed contract language.

Legal has advised a few redlines (attached as "proposed-security-exhibit-redlines.docx") to avoid broad "unfettered inspection" language — Karthik will follow up with the specific MSA wording.

Proposed next step: Laura, Karthik and I can join a 30-minute call with your procurement on Thursday 5/21 at 10am ET if that works. If you prefer, we can push a marked-up MSA and short rationale first.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Head of Trust Operations | Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.ai
[Attachments: proposed-security-exhibit-redlines.docx (docx), evidence-ownership-matrix.csv (csv)]

Hi all — looping in legal comments for the MSA redline. I reviewed Mina's operational proposals and suggest the following contract edits to the audit rights clause and security exhibit. These are intentionally narrow to preserve customer assurance while protecting Redwood's production environment. Proposed clauses: 

1) Scope and Notice: Replace "at any time" audit language with: "Customer may request an inspection during a mutually agreed inspection window. Customer must provide no less than thirty (30) calendar days' prior written notice for any on-site or remote inspection, unless otherwise mutually agreed in writing."

2) Sampling and Evidence: Add: "Redwood will provide a representative sample of logs and artifacts reasonably necessary to demonstrate compliance with the applicable control framework. Where full exports are requested, Redwood will provide filtered or redacted data and may charge for additional processing time."

3) Penetration Testing: Insert process flow: test plan submission (>=21 days prior), Redwood response within 7 business days, mutually-agreed testing window, mandatory coordination with Redwood SRE, and prohibition on testing that impacts production availability. Include requirement that Customer provide proof of insurance and sign an agreed Test Authorization form prior to the test.

4) Safe Harbor & Vulnerability Disclosure: Include a vulnerability disclosure channel, engagement SLA for triage, and a remediation window for validated issues. For critical flaws posing immediate risk, Redwood will agree an accelerated review and patch plan; for liability purposes both parties acknowledge the limited scope of liability tied to commercial indemnities in the MSA.

I attached a marked-up MSA excerpt (redlines) and a one-page rationale labeled "MSA-exhibit-rationale.pdf". Operational teams: please confirm the 21/7/30 timelines work or propose alternates.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Thanks Karthik and Mina — this reads well and is much closer to what procurement/legal need. A few quick notes from our side: 

- Procurement prefers a 30-day notice but will accept a 21-day test-plan submission if Redwood is committing to the 7-business-day review SLA. Can we confirm that in the exhibit text?
- For evidence exports, HealthScope needs the ability to request a deeper export for compliance audits (we don't expect this often). If Redwood will provide a filtered export under an executed NDA and a documented request, procurement is comfortable with a cost-recovery fee.
- Could you add a sentence to the pen-test workflow that says the customer must cease testing if Redwood observes any adverse impact and that Redwood will provide a point-of-contact for any escalation during the test?

We have a small procurement PO attached; this is to reserve budget while legal finalizes the redlines (not a signed order). Also could we schedule the 30-minute call Thursday 5/21 at 10am ET — that works for Ben and me.
